title: Pain au Levain (Sourdough Bread)
steps: LEVAIN BUILD (12 hours before mixing): Combine 130g bread flour, 9g rye flour, 85g water, and 28g mature stiff culture. Mix well, cover, and let ripen at 21°C for ~12 hours. In hot weather, or if ripening longer than 12 hours, add a pinch of salt (1.8% of levain flour) to slow activity.
AUTOLYSE: Combine all final dough flour (731g bread flour + 37g rye flour) with 505g water in a mixing bowl. Mix on low speed just until a shaggy mass forms. Cover and rest 20–60 minutes.

MIXING: Sprinkle 17g salt over the dough surface. Cut the ripened levain into fist-sized pieces and place on top. Mix on second speed for 1½–2 minutes until smooth and supple. Target dough temperature: 24°C.
BULK FERMENTATION: Cover and ferment at room temperature for 2½ hours.
FOLDING: Fold the dough twice during bulk fermentation — first fold at 50 minutes, second fold at 100 minutes.

DIVIDING & SHAPING: Divide dough into two equal pieces (~680g each). Pre-shape gently and rest 20 minutes. Shape each piece into a round (boule) or oval (bâtard). Place seam-side up in floured bannetons.
FINAL FERMENTATION: Ferment at 24°C for 2–2½ hours, or retard overnight in the refrigerator (not recommended — loses delicate flavour).

BAKING: Preheat oven to 225°C with a Dutch oven or baking stone. Bake with steam for the first 15 minutes, then remove steam source and bake a further 25–30 minutes until deep russet brown. Total bake time: 40–45 minutes. Cool completely on a wire rack before cutting.
tips: A stiff levain (60% hydration) gives this bread its French character: open crumb, russet crust, and delicate flavour. Bake the same day — retarding overnight dulls the subtle notes. 95% bread flour + 5% rye is the classic formula; the rye feeds the levain and adds colour.
